title: Who can see a member: the access table

blocks.text: Java has four access levels. The page's own examples declare one member at each:
Write `AccessTable.canAccess(Level level, From from)`. It answers whether code in the place `from` may use a member declared with `level`.
`From` names where the using code sits, relative to the class that declares the member:

items: `NESTED_CLASS`: inside a class nested in the same top-level class;
`SAME_PACKAGE`: in another class of the same package;
`SUBCLASS_OTHER_PACKAGE`: in a subclass that lives in a different package;
`OTHER_PACKAGE`: in an unrelated class of a different package.

blocks.text:
canAccess(PUBLIC,  OTHER_PACKAGE)   -> true
canAccess(PRIVATE, SAME_PACKAGE)    -> false
canAccess(PRIVATE, SAME_CLASS)      -> true
Mind the two levels in the middle: read the page's definitions of protected and package-private carefully.

cases.says: A public member is visible from everywhere, and a private one only inside its own class.
A protected member is visible to any class in the same package, not only to subclasses.
A package-private member is hidden from a subclass that lives in another package.
A class nested in the same top-level class can use its private members.

origin.section: Detailed Explanation of Each Access Modifier

concepts: Public is visible everywhere, protected in the package and in subclasses, package-private in the package only, and private in the class only.
Protected also opens a member to every class in the same package, not only to subclasses.
